cells.tense: You're here with your hands on it, reading the shape of something before all of it has shown itself.
cells.ask: Let one thing you've figured out reach someone as a feeling before it reaches them as a conclusion.
cells.core:
This part of your life is where you work without a full picture. You read what's actually there — the pieces in front of you, the direction they lean — and you move from that, not from a plan that covers everything. You can hold a question open and still act. That's rare and it's working.

The edge you're standing on is that all this reading could stay in your head, where it does no one any good. Let one thing you've understood land as something a person can feel, not just follow. The understanding is already yours; let it be shared.
cells.sheetLine: You read what's really there and move from it, without needing the whole picture first.
cells.verb: cutting through what's blurred to the pattern underneath
cells.place: in the place where not enough is known yet and the next step still has to be taken

cells.tense: You're leaning into what's coming, trying to have the whole answer worked out before it's even asked of you.
cells.ask: Pick the one part that has to be settled now, settle that, and let the rest stay open a while longer.
cells.core:
Working without a full picture is what this part of your life asks, and usually you're good at it — you read the pieces you have and move. Right now you've stopped moving and started bracing. You're running the pattern forward in every direction, trying to have the end already decided before the beginning has finished happening. More certainty is not arriving no matter how hard you work for it.

What's missing isn't more analysis. It's structure — one decision made cleanly, with a shape to it, so the rest can rest. Not the whole road laid out. One piece settled, well.

cells.tense: There was a point where you stopped trusting your own read, and you're still standing at that point.
cells.ask: Give one person the rough version of something you've been keeping to yourself, and let their response shape it.
cells.core:
Reading a situation before it's clear is what this part of your life is for, and the way through is noticing what's actually there — the pattern under the surface — and taking the next step from that. You can do this. You've done it.

What stopped is the sharing of it. Somewhere the read you had didn't get said out loud, or didn't land the way you needed it to, and since then you've kept it in. The perceiving hasn't gone anywhere. The handing-over has. What's missing isn't insight. It's putting a half-formed version in front of another person and letting the conversation do the rest.
cells.sheetLine: You still see the pattern. You've just stopped saying what you see.

cells.tense: You're already steering through the unclear part with your own read, and calling it something other than steering.
cells.ask: Say out loud, once, that you know what you know about one situation you've been treating as still undecided.
cells.core:
This part of your life asks you to move through the unclear, and when it goes well you read the surface, find the shape beneath it, and act on what you find — knowing it's you who found it. That's the capacity running clean.

Right now the reading is still happening, but the conclusion gets described as though it arrived on its own and you're just passing it along. You did the seeing. You did the cutting through. What's left is to claim that, in front of someone, once. Not the analysis — the fact that it came from you.
